\label{lemma-vanishing-lqc}
In Situation \ref{situation-global}.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a locally quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-module
on $\text{Cris}(X/S)$. Then we have
$$
H^p((U, T, \delta), \mathcal{F}) = 0
$$
for all $p > 0$ and all $(U, T, \delta)$ with $T$ or $U$ affine.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

For an object $(U,T,\delta)$ in the small crystalline site, $H^j((U,T,\delta),\mathcal F)$ denotes sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal F$ on the slice site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)/(U,T,\delta)$. For the full site, $R\Gamma(\mathrm{Cris}(X/S),\mathcal F)$ denotes derived global sections. If $\mathcal F$ is locally quasi-coherent, its restriction $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent on $T$.

Under the global crystalline setup above,
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a locally quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-module
on $\text{Cris}(X/S)$. Then we have
$$
H^p((U, T, \delta), \mathcal{F}) = 0
$$
for all $p > 0$ and all $(U, T, \delta)$ with $T$ or $U$ affine.

\label{lemma-compare}
In Situation \ref{situation-global}.
Assume moreover $X$ and $S$ are affine schemes.
Consider the full subcategory $\mathcal{C} \subset \text{Cris}(X/S)$
consisting of divided power thickenings $(X, T, \delta)$
endowed with the chaotic topology (see
Sites, Example \ref{sites-example-indiscrete}).
For any locally quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-module $\mathcal{F}$
we have
$$
R\Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}|_\mathcal{C}) =
R\Gamma(\text{Cris}(X/S), \mathcal{F})
$$

The chaotic (indiscrete) topology on a category is the Grothendieck topology in which only maximal sieves cover; every presheaf is a sheaf. If an object $Y$ receives a map from every object and finite products exist, the augmented Cech complex of $Y$ has degree-$n$ terms $\mathcal F(Y^{n+1})$, with the coface maps induced by omission of factors. The derived global sections of an abelian sheaf are represented by this complex when the resulting Cech terms are acyclic.

R\Gamma(\text{Cris}(X/S), \mathcal{F})
$$

\label{lemma-complete}
In Situation \ref{situation-affine}.
Set $\mathcal{C} = (\text{Cris}(C/A))^{opp}$ and
$\mathcal{C}^\wedge = (\text{Cris}^\wedge(C/A))^{opp}$
endowed with the chaotic topology, see
Remark \ref{remark-completed-affine-site} for notation.
There is a morphism of topoi
$$
g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \longrightarrow \Sh(\mathcal{C}^\wedge)
$$
such that if $\mathcal{F}$ is a sheaf of abelian groups on
$\mathcal{C}$, then
$$
R^pg_*\mathcal{F}(B \to C, \delta) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\lim_e \mathcal{F}(B_e \to C, \delta) & \text{if }p = 0 \\
R^1\lim_e \mathcal{F}(B_e \to C, \delta) & \text{if }p = 1 \\
0 & \text{else}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
where $B_e = B/p^eB$ for $e \gg 0$.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ with $A$ a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-algebra, together with an $A$-algebra $C$ such that $IC=0$ and $p$ is nilpotent in $C$. An object of $\mathrm{CRIS}(C/A)$ is a divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra $(B,J_B,\delta)$ with $p$ nilpotent in $B$ and a compatible $A$-algebra map $C\to B/J_B$; morphisms preserve the divided powers and this map from $C$. The full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ consists of objects with $C\cong B/J_B$. The completed category $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ has analogously compatible objects complete for the $p$-adic topology, with divided powers extended to the completion; for sufficiently large $e$, reductions $B/p^eB$ lie in $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$.

For an affine crystalline datum $(A,I,\gamma)\to C$ with $p$ nilpotent on $C$, let $\mathrm{Cris}(C/A)$ be the category of divided power $A$-algebras $(B,J,\delta)$ with quotient isomorphic to $C$, $p$ nilpotent in $B$. Let $\mathrm{Cris}^\wedge(C/A)$ be the analogous category of $p$-adically complete such divided power algebras. Put $\mathcal C=(\mathrm{Cris}(C/A))^{op}$ and $\mathcal C^\wedge=(\mathrm{Cris}^\wedge(C/A))^{op}$, both with chaotic topologies. For a completed object $(B,J,\delta)$ put $B_e=B/p^eB$ (for sufficiently large $e$). The right-derived inverse limit of a tower of abelian groups has $\varprojlim$ in degree $0$ and $R^1\!\varprojlim$ in degree $1$, with no higher derived inverse limits for a tower indexed by the positive integers.

Under the affine crystalline setup above,
Set $\mathcal{C} = (\text{Cris}(C/A))^{opp}$ and
$\mathcal{C}^\wedge = (\text{Cris}^\wedge(C/A))^{opp}$
endowed with the chaotic topology, with $\mathrm{Cris}^{\wedge}(C/A)$ the category of $p$-adically complete divided power thickenings defined above.
There is a morphism of topoi
$$
g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \longrightarrow \Sh(\mathcal{C}^\wedge)
$$
such that if $\mathcal{F}$ is a sheaf of abelian groups on
$\mathcal{C}$, then
$$
R^pg_*\mathcal{F}(B \to C, \delta) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\lim_e \mathcal{F}(B_e \to C, \delta) & \text{if }p = 0 \\
R^1\lim_e \mathcal{F}(B_e \to C, \delta) & \text{if }p = 1 \\
0 & \text{else}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
where $B_e = B/p^eB$ for $e \gg 0$.
